narrative:
The model estimated a 65% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a majority risk, so the law school denied your application because it judged your likely bar outcome too uncertain to admit.

The strongest reason was your first-year class-rank decile of 1, far below the average of 6 among admitted students; this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.30, also below the admitted average of 3.23, was the second most influential factor and likewise pushed toward failure. The third factor, your full-time status, leaned slightly toward passing and therefore did not drive the rejection.

To improve a future application, ask admissions for specific feedback, consider retaking the LSAT and strengthening your academic record through additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate program, and explain any first-year circumstances. Focus on demonstrating sustained academic improvement and bar-exam readiness before reapplying.
